{"markdown":"# Issues Memo — Master Services Agreement

**Prepared for:** Customer (internal)  
**Subject:** Playbook review of the Master Services Agreement  
**Privileged & Confidential — Attorney Work Product**

---

## 1. Executive summary

The Agreement is, on the whole, strongly aligned with our playbook. Nineteen rules were assessed: seventeen are compliant and two are deviations. Several clauses sit at or above our preferred position, including Vendor indemnification with indemnities carved out of the liability cap (§ 20, § 21.3), Customer ownership of Deliverables and Customer Data with a perpetual licence to embedded Vendor Technology (§ 14), unrestricted termination for convenience on thirty days' notice with refund of prepaid Fees (§ 9.4), and post-termination transition assistance at expiring Order Form rates (§ 11). There is no exclusivity, non-compete, minimum-commitment, customer-side MFN, or non-solicit burden on Customer, and the only competition covenant runs against Vendor (§ 12.3–12.4).

Two items require negotiation, and both sit in walk-away territory as drafted:

1. **Liability cap quantum (§ 21.1).** The cap is mutual and the carve-outs are good, but "Fees" is defined by reference to the one-time USD 12,000 Implementation Fee in the first Order Form. The effective cap is therefore approximately USD 12,000 regardless of subscription spend — below even six months' charges.
2. **Customer-payable liquidated damages (§ 7.7).** Fifteen percent of annual Fees per week of late payment, triggered by a ten-day delay, uncapped and compounding, and expressly outside the liability cap by operation of § 21.3.

Both are fixable with narrow, single-point edits; we do not need to reopen the surrounding architecture of either section.

---

## 2. Findings

| Severity | Rule | Status | Section |
|---|---|---|---|
| Critical | INDEMN — Indemnification by Vendor | Compliant | § 20 Indemnification |
| Critical | IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data | Compliant | § 14 Intellectual Property and Deliverables |
| High | ASSIGN — Assignment and change of control | Compliant | § 24 Assignment and Change of Control |
| High | EXCLUSIVITY — Exclusivity obligations binding Customer | Compliant | § 12 Customer Responsibilities |
| High | LICENSE — Licence grant scope | Compliant | § 13 Access Rights and Licence |
| High | NONCOMPETE — Non-compete restrictions on Customer | Compliant | § 12 Customer Responsibilities |
| High | T4C — Termination for convenience | Compliant | § 9 Termination |
| Medium | **LOL-CAP — Limitation of liability (cap, mutuality, carve-outs)** | **Deviation** | § 21 Limitation of Liability |
| Medium | AUDIT — Audit rights against Customer | Compliant | § 22 Audit Rights |
| Medium | GOVLAW — Governing law and venue | Compliant | § 28 Governing Law and Dispute Resolution |
| Medium | MFN — Most-favoured-nation obligations burdening Customer | Compliant | § 7 Fees, Invoicing, and Taxes |
| Medium | MINCOMMIT — Minimum purchase commitments and volume restrictions | Compliant | § 2 Agreement Structure and Scope |
| Medium | NOSOLICIT — Non-solicitation of employees binding Customer | Compliant | § 12 Customer Responsibilities |
| Medium | RENEWAL — Auto-renewal and non-renewal notice window | Compliant | § 8 Term and Renewal |
| Medium | TRANSITION — Post-termination transition assistance and data return | Compliant | § 11 Transition Assistance and Data Return |
| Medium | WARRANTY — Performance warranty and duration | Compliant | § 19 Warranties |
| Low | INSURANCE — Vendor insurance | Compliant | § 18 Insurance |
| Low | **LD — Liquidated damages and penalties payable by Customer** | **Deviation** | § 7 Fees, Invoicing, and Taxes |

### 2.1 Deviation detail

**§ 21.1 — Limitation of liability cap (medium).** Mutuality, the mutual exclusion of indirect damages (§ 21.2), and the Excluded Claims list (§ 21.3 — confidentiality, data protection and security, indemnities, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud, IP infringement) are all at or above our preferred position, and Customer's payment obligation is expressly not "damages." The problem is quantum only: "Fees" is defined at § 1.5 as the Implementation Fee, itself defined at § 1.8 as "the one-time implementation charge of USD 12,000 stated in the first Order Form," and § 21.1 further limits the basis to the first Order Form. Our proposal is the minimal fix: rebase § 21.1 on all amounts paid or payable under the Agreement and all Order Forms in the twelve months preceding the claim, with the USD 1,000,000 limb, and confirm that all amounts due are not damages. No other part of § 21 is touched.

**§ 7.7 — Customer-payable liquidated damages (low severity, high commercial exposure).** Our playbook position is that no liquidated damages or penalties are payable by Customer; the fallback permits only a capped early-termination fee, which this is not. The charge compounds weekly without a cap from a ten-day (potentially inadvertent) delay and is not constrained by § 21, since § 21.3 places payment obligations outside the cap. We propose a single operative edit negating the liquidated damages and substituting customary late-payment interest on undisputed overdue invoices, which reaches the preferred position while leaving Vendor a proportionate remedy. Service credits and SLA remedies running in Customer's favour are unaffected.

---

## 3. Walk-away items

We should not sign in the current form on either of the following:

1. **§ 21.1 liability cap of approximately USD 12,000.** A cap keyed to the one-time Implementation Fee is illusory relative to subscription spend and falls below the six-month floor. Resolution: rebase on twelve months' fees paid or payable across all Order Forms, with the USD 1,000,000 limb.
2. **§ 7.7 uncapped, weekly-compounding liquidated damages payable by Customer.** The charge can exceed remaining contract value and is a penalty in substance notwithstanding the label. Resolution: delete and replace with late-payment interest on undisputed overdue invoices.

---

## 4. Next steps

1. Issue the two redlines described above (§ 21.1 rebasing; § 7.7 replacement) and hold the balance of § 21 and § 7 as drafted.
2. Confirm with the business the expected annual subscription spend so we can validate that the twelve-month/USD 1,000,000 construct in § 21.1 is adequate for this engagement.
3. Confirm internally that Vendor's payment terms are operationally achievable, so that the substituted late-payment interest mechanic in § 7.7 is a workable landing zone.
4. Circulate the memo to the deal team, flagging the two walk-away items as conditions to signature; no further diligence is required on the seventeen compliant rules.
5. On countersignature, calendar the § 8.2 renewal reminder and thirty-day opt-out window, and the § 11 thirty-day data-return request mechanic, for contract administration."}
